items.prompt: Я обязательно _____ этот проект к пятнице. (definite commitment to finish)
items.promptEnglish: I will definitely finish this project by Friday.
items.hint: A definite commitment to a result uses perfective.
items.explanation: Обязательно + deadline = definite commitment. Perfective закончу signals guaranteed completion.

items.hint: General truths about the natural world use imperfective.
items.explanation: Universal biological facts take imperfective present: живут.

items.prompt: Ты вечно _____ свои вещи! (annoyance at a repeated habit)
items.hint: Criticism of a repeated annoying action uses imperfective.
items.explanation: Repeated irritating habit = imperfective теряешь. The adverb вечно reinforces the pattern.

items.prompt: Не волнуйся, я _____ тебе. (a definite, specific offer)
items.promptEnglish: Don't worry, I'll help you. (firm offer)
items.hint: A firm, specific offer to help uses perfective.
items.explanation: Definite offer = perfective помогу. Imperfective буду помогать would sound vaguer.

items.prompt: Я _____ тебе завтра, обещаю. (a specific promise to call)
items.promptEnglish: I'll call you tomorrow, I promise.
items.hint: A concrete promise to perform a specific action uses perfective.
items.explanation: Обещаю + perfective позвоню = committed promise. Буду звонить would imply repeated calling, not one firm action.

minimalPairs.context: Завтра я _____ статью. (commitment to produce a result)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Tomorrow I will write the article. (will definitely complete it)
minimalPairs.explanation: Perfective напишу = guaranteed completion. The speaker commits to having a finished article.

minimalPairs.context: Завтра я _____ статью. (process, no guarantee of finishing)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Tomorrow I'll be writing an article. (working on it, might not finish)
minimalPairs.explanation: Imperfective буду писать = process. The speaker plans to work on it but makes no promise about completion.

minimalPairs.context: Она всегда _____ двери! (criticism of a habit)
minimalPairs.explanation: Imperfective хлопает + всегда = annoyance at a repeated habit.
General truths about species take imperfective present: любят.

sets.title: Fix and Translate
sets.description: Correct aspect errors and translate sentences with the right nuance
sets.descriptionRussian: Исправьте ошибки и переведите предложения с правильным нюансом

errorCorrection.hint: Criticism of a repeated habit uses imperfective, not perfective.
errorCorrection.explanation: Repeated annoying habit = imperfective: теряешь. Потеряешь (pf future) would mean a single future event.

translation.english: I will definitely send you the documents tomorrow.
translation.answer: Я обязательно отправлю тебе документы завтра.
acceptableVariants: Завтра я обязательно отправлю тебе документы.
Я обязательно пришлю тебе документы завтра.

translation.english: Birds fly south in winter. (general fact)
She's always complaining about the weather!
translation.hint: Annoyance at repeated behavior = вечно/всегда + imperfective

items.prompt: Which nuance does this sentence express? "Он постоянно разговаривает по телефону!"
items.promptEnglish: He's constantly talking on the phone!
items.hint: Постоянно + imperfective = what type of nuance?
items.explanation: Постоянно + imperfective = frustration at a repeated habit. The speaker is annoyed.

items.prompt: Which nuance does this sentence express? "Я решу этот вопрос сегодня."
items.hint: Perfective with a deadline suggests a firm commitment.
items.explanation: Решу (perfective) + today = definite commitment to produce a result.

items.prompt: Which nuance does this sentence express? "Снег тает весной."
items.hint: A statement about what happens every spring is a general truth.
items.explanation: Imperfective present тает describing a natural phenomenon = general fact.

sets.title: Pairs and Patterns
sets.description: Compare aspect pairs and identify patterns in nuance usage
sets.descriptionRussian: Сравните видовые пары и определите закономерности

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ тебе ответ завтра. (firm promise to give a result)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I'll give you the answer tomorrow. (definite commitment)
minimalPairs.explanation: Perfective дам = definite, one-time result. Буду давать would imply repeated giving.

minimalPairs.context: Она _____ на совещаниях. (habitual behavior, speaker annoyed)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: She always falls asleep at meetings! (annoying habit)
minimalPairs.explanation: Imperfective засыпает = repeated annoying habit. Заснёт (pf) = single future event.
General scientific fact = imperfective present расширяется.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ этот документ к обеду. (firm deadline commitment)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I'll prepare this document by lunch. (definite)
minimalPairs.explanation: Definite commitment with deadline к обеду = perfective подготовлю.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: He's always telling other people's secrets! (annoyed)
minimalPairs.explanation: Вечно + imperfective = annoyance at repeated behavior.

patternRecognition.sentence: Я обязательно сделаю. / Я тебе помогу. / Я всё объясню.
patternRecognition.question: What do all three sentences have in common?
patternRecognition.explanation: All three use perfective future (сделаю, помогу, объясню) to express firm promises or commitments.

patternRecognition.sentence: Ты опять опаздываешь! / Он вечно жалуется! / Она постоянно забывает!
patternRecognition.question: What unifies these three sentences?
options: They express annoyance at repeated behavior (imperfective)
patternRecognition.answer: They express annoyance at repeated behavior (imperfective)
patternRecognition.explanation: All use imperfective present + time adverbs (опять, вечно, постоянно) to express irritation at habits.

patternRecognition.sentence: Земля вращается. / Вода кипит при 100°. / Снег тает весной.
patternRecognition.question: What aspect nuance do these sentences share?
patternRecognition.explanation: All describe universal truths using imperfective present tense.

blanks: Не беспокойся, я всё _____. (Don't worry, I'll take care of everything.)
Почему он постоянно _____?! (Why does he constantly interrupt?!)
Реки _____ в моря. (Rivers flow into seas.)
hints: A reassuring promise to handle everything = perfective.
explanations: Firm commitment: perfective сделаю - 'I will get it done.'
Annoyance: imperfective перебивает with постоянно = frustration at interruptions.
General geographical fact: imperfective впадают - rivers flow into seas as a rule.

items.prompt: Я _____ этот вопрос на собрании. (firm intention to raise it)
items.promptEnglish: I will raise this issue at the meeting. (definite plan)
items.hint: A definite plan to perform a specific action = perfective.
items.explanation: Committed plan = perfective подниму. Буду поднимать would imply repeatedly raising it.
Вечно + imperfective жалуется = irritation at her constant complaining.

items.prompt: Она опять _____ чужую еду из холодильника! (annoyed)
items.promptEnglish: She's eating other people's food from the fridge again!
items.explanation: Repeated frustrating action: imperfective ест + опять.

items.prompt: Я обещаю, я _____ всё к сроку. (firm promise)
items.promptEnglish: I promise, I'll finish everything on time.
items.hint: Обещаю + deadline = perfective for firm commitment.
items.explanation: Promise + deadline: perfective сделаю for guaranteed completion.

items.promptEnglish: In winter, the days get shorter. (general pattern)
items.hint: A recurring natural pattern = imperfective present.
items.explanation: Recurring seasonal fact: imperfective становятся - this happens every winter.

errorCorrection.hint: Criticism of a repeated habit requires imperfective, not perfective.
errorCorrection.explanation: Всегда + annoyance = imperfective опаздываешь. Опоздаешь (pf) would describe a single future event.

errorCorrection.sentence: Не переживай, я буду решать эту проблему. (meant as a firm reassurance)
errorCorrection.hint: Firm reassurance uses perfective to show commitment.
errorCorrection.explanation: To reassure someone with a definite commitment: perfective решу. Буду решать sounds uncommitted.
